name: Kaushik Parthasarathy
title: Software Engineer | Backend and Distributed Systems
bio:
Most of what I build starts with a gap. Something I haven't worked with yet, or something I want to understand by building it instead of just reading about it. Lately that gap has been systems that have to stay correct when part of them fails.

Atlas is the clearest example. I built a ride-dispatch backend as three gRPC microservices on Kubernetes, in Java because I was learning it at the time, then killed a live pod mid-ramp to 500 req/s on a routing stub. 0.00% of 101,249 requests failed and no trip was duplicated. Quantico came from the same instinct, a Python research pipeline with a C++ execution simulator, built so that a "no edge" result can actually be trusted.

At Wells Fargo, I worked across the stack on portfolio management systems handling $400B+ in assets, from React to .NET APIs to OpenShift. I designed a deployment architecture that made deploys 3x faster and was adopted by 4 other React apps in the division, and I ran on-call for production. At ISRO, I cut per-frame latency in a computer vision pipeline from 20s to 2s by running five models as concurrent REST services.

Python is what I reach for first, but I adapt to whatever the problem calls for. I didn't know .NET going into Wells Fargo, and I learned Java for Atlas.

Currently pursuing an MS in Computer Science at UMass Amherst. Open to full-time software engineering roles.
